title: Weil group after a finite constant-field extension
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a
separated finite-type
$\mathbf F_q$-scheme with geometrically connected fibre
$X=X_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. For $m\geq1$,
put

$$
X_0^{(m)}=X_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}\mathbf F_{q^m}
$$

and regard it as an $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-scheme. Under the natural map to
$X_0$, its Weil group identifies with

$$
W(X_0^{(m)})
\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}
W(X_0)^{[m]}:=\deg^{-1}(m\mathbf Z)\subseteq W(X_0).
$$

Its geometric subgroup is still $\pi_1(X)$, and its normalized degree is

$$
\deg_{\mathbf F_{q^m}}(w)=\deg_{\mathbf F_q}(w)/m.
$$

In particular, if $s\in W(X_0)$ has degree one, then $s^m$ has degree
one for the $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-Weil group.

proof.text: The scheme $X_0^{(m)}$ is separated and of finite type over $\mathbf F_{q^m}$ (base change of the separated finite-type $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_q$ along $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^m}\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_q$), and its geometric fibre $X_0^{(m)}\times_{\mathbf F_{q^m}}\overline{\mathbf F}_q=X_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}\overline{\mathbf F}_q=X$ is connected, so $X_0^{(m)}$ is a geometrically connected separated finite-type $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-scheme and its Weil group and degree are defined. Apply [lem-wf-weil-group-constant-extension-pi1-base-change] to the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. It identifies the arithmetic fundamental group of $X_0^{(m)}$ with the inverse image of $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf F}_q/\mathbf F_{q^m})$ in the arithmetic fundamental group of $X_0$, and identifies the geometric kernel with the same $\pi_1(X)$. Restricting the inverse image to the infinite cyclic subgroup generated by the relevant geometric Frobenius gives the natural map of Weil groups.

By the convention of [def-tw-frobenius-action], geometric Frobenius over $\mathbf F_{q^m}$ is the $m$-th power of geometric Frobenius over $\mathbf F_q$. Using the inverse-image description from [lem-wf-weil-group-constant-extension-pi1-base-change] together with the definition of the Weil group and degree map in [def-wf-weil-group], the resulting subgroup is exactly $W(X_0)^{[m]}=\deg^{-1}(m\mathbf Z)$. The exact sequence [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence] identifies its degree-zero subgroup with $\pi_1(X)$ and shows that the old degree divided by $m$ is the normalized degree over $\mathbf F_{q^m}$. In particular, a degree-one element $s$ has $s^m$ of normalized degree one.
